skill.name: bun
skill.description: Use Bun instead of Node.js, npm, pnpm, or vite. Provides command mappings, Bun-specific APIs, and development patterns.
skill.summary: A practical guide for using Bun commands, APIs, testing, servers, databases, and development workflows.
skill.author: brianlovin

security_audit.summary: All 28 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code spans, examples, and API documentation in SKILL.md. No evidence found of executed commands, secret exfiltration, prompt injection, or reconnaissance behavior.

remediation.issue: The documented Bun shell command API can execute external processes when used with untrusted input.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to keep command names fixed, pass untrusted values as parameters, and validate input before invoking shell commands.

remediation.issue: Bun automatically loads environment files, which can expose secrets to application code.
remediation.suggestion: Document secret minimization, local-only environment files, and exclusion of environment files from source control.

content.value_statement: Developers often maintain separate Node.js tools, scripts, and configuration for common workflows. This skill maps those workflows to Bun and explains Bun APIs for faster application development.
actual_capabilities: Maps common Node.js, npm, pnpm, Vite, and testing commands to Bun equivalents.
Explains Bun APIs for HTTP servers, WebSockets, databases, files, and shell commands.
Shows how to write tests with bun:test.
Demonstrates Bun.serve patterns for routes, React, CSS, and HTML imports.
Explains Bun bundling and hot reload workflows for JavaScript, TypeScript, JSX, and TSX.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not install Bun or modify a project automatically.
It does not replace framework-specific documentation or production deployment guidance.
Examples may require a compatible Bun version and project configuration.
It does not audit application code for vulnerabilities.

use_cases.title: Migrate a Node.js Project
use_cases.description: Translate package, test, build, and development commands from Node.js tooling to Bun.

use_cases.title: Create a Bun Web Server
use_cases.description: Plan a small server with Bun.serve, routes, WebSockets, HTML imports, and hot reload.

use_cases.title: Set Up Bun Testing
use_cases.description: Convert basic tests to bun:test and choose a practical command for running the test suite.

prompt_templates.title: Map My Commands
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert these Node.js and npm commands to Bun equivalents. Preserve the intent and explain any important differences: [paste commands].

prompt_templates.title: Explain a Bun API
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to use this Bun API in a small TypeScript project. Include the purpose, required setup, and one concise usage example: [API name].

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bun Server
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bun.serve structure for this application. Cover routes, static assets, WebSockets if needed, environment configuration, and local development commands: [application details].

prompt_templates.title: Review a Bun Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project migration from Node.js to Bun. Identify incompatible assumptions, command changes, test changes, environment concerns, and a staged validation plan: [project details].

output_examples.input: Replace npm install, npm test, and npm run dev with Bun commands.
output: Use bun install for dependency installation.
Use bun test for the test suite.
Use bun run dev for the development script.

output_examples.input: Which Bun API should serve a small application with routes and WebSockets?
output_examples.output: Use Bun.serve as the central server API. Define routes for HTTP requests and add a WebSocket handler when the application needs persistent client connections.

output_examples.input: How should a team validate a move from Node.js to Bun?
output_examples.output: Run the existing tests, compare dependency behavior, verify environment loading, exercise build and development commands, and test production-like server paths.

best_practices: Check Bun version compatibility before changing project commands or APIs.
Keep environment files private and document required variables without exposing secret values.
Validate migrated tests, builds, routes, and database behavior before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every Node.js dependency behaves identically under Bun.
Do not place secrets in source files, examples, or committed environment files.
Do not pass untrusted input directly into shell commands.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It explains Bun commands, APIs, testing, servers, bundling, and common development workflows.

faq.question: Can it migrate my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides migration guidance and review support, but it does not edit files or run commands.

faq.question: Does it replace Node.js documentation?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Bun equivalents and Bun-specific patterns. Consult official documentation for unsupported or version-specific behavior.

faq.question: Can it help build an HTTP server?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Bun.serve, routes, static assets, WebSockets, HTML imports, and local development.

faq.question: Does it support testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers bun:test and command mappings for running test suites.

faq.question: Is it a security scanner?
faq.answer: No. It offers basic safety guidance, but it does not perform a complete application security audit.
